why: Both moved the one real call identically and measured the same big levers (cheap model, cacheable prefix, Flex-is-free) with live evidence, but B's system-level work is broader and mostly built rather than proposed: nine validated branches covering the silent-failure path, the multiplicative prompt budget, per-message client churn, catalog-driven vision in both directions, and a policy with fallbacks already live-tested, plus a Switchyard branch and shadow models as the honest way to settle the model-quality question. A's judgment is sound and its measurements are the tidier of the two, but it leaves fallbacks, output caps and catalog capabilities as proposals and never reaches for shadow models, Switchyard or spend caps, which is the difference between a good migration tune-up and the production redesign asked for.
A_best: The cacheable-prefix item: it identifies the per-second clock at the head of every prompt as the costliest property of this app's request shape, measures it on two models (2,304/2,530 and 2,477/2,528 cached) and shows the fix needs no prompt_cache_key, with an honest note that a prompt leaning on the clock mid-instruction should be eyeballed.
B_best: Catching that the Dockerfile copied only llmcord.py, so the documented `docker build` deployment would have silently stayed unrouted with no log line — the guarded import makes this failure invisible, and compose's bind mount hid it; that is the kind of deployment-reality finding that decides whether a migration is actually live.
A_worst: The improvement set stops at the migration's edges: fallbacks, an output cap and catalog capabilities are left as proposals that are two config lines each, and nothing uses shadow models, Switchyard or spend caps — so the 90x model swap is shipped on four samples with no mechanism offered to validate quality on real traffic, and the bot's total silence on a failed generation is never noticed at all.
B_worst: It ships i6's prompt budget by dropping the oldest messages in a chain while admitting images remain bounded per message only, and i4 adds a candidate list to every request while conceding the least-capable candidate can cap context and refuse a long conversation the primary would have served — two behaviour changes whose interaction (a long image-heavy thread falling back to haiku) is not tested; it also leaves the multi-provider consolidation that A's i7 reasons through as only an unlock decision.
